headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Cutting and Framing Exterior Window Openings
articleBody:
Framing an exterior window requires balancing structural loads with weatherproofing. Small oversights during the rough framing phase can cause costly water damage or sticking windows. Here are the main errors to avoid before work starts.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Sizing from glass dimensions: Ordering framing based on glass area rather than full window-frame unit dimensions creates openings that are far too small. Always check the manufacturer's rough-opening guide.
- Leaving insufficient clearance for shims: Building an opening that is too tight leaves no room to shim the frame plumb and square, which leads to binding window sashes.
- Skipping diagonal measurements: An opening can appear plumb on both sides yet still be racked. Measuring corner to corner diagonally is essential to guarantee a true rectangle.
- Mismanaging the sill drainage path: Level sills are standard, but blocking sill pan drainage or reverse-lapping flashing materials traps moisture inside the wall assembly.
- Neglecting overhead structural loads: Using undersized headers across exterior window spans causes sagging, putting downward pressure on the window unit that can crack glass or break seals.
- Relying on shims to fix bad framing: Shims are designed for micro-adjustments, not to bridge half-inch framing mistakes or out-of-plumb studs.

What Can Change the Right Choice
The siding material, wall thickness, and whether you are installing a flanged new-construction unit or a replacement frame determine framing depth and flashing integration. For dependable framing craftsmanship, contact Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
